notes: The author writes five relations under(10), including rho cubed equals1 and the product of three squared epsilons equals1. Three later rows retain cancelled prefactors/exponents and cancelled rho-like factors. The marginal addition says that conjugation relations must also be added, with the explicit reservation au moins!, and says there are two generators. These statements are transcribed as claims rather than verified here.

The author explicitly asks whether rho is expressible in terms of the epsilons and writes that, as before, the answer is no. Root alerted the reader to a possible conflict between this statement and the first surviving product. The entire first product and following sentence were inspected on separate complete crops; the live exponent4 and que non are retained. No algebraic verification was performed by this reader; root will record its scoped checks separately.

The subsequent discussion says there is no privileged path from P to barP for lifting dotted tau, but there are three equally natural choices. The author prefers to consider the isotropy subgroup and writes the lift of dotted sigma, the homomorphism(11), its canonical lift(12), and the final tilde-sigma_i definition. The wording je préfère and the author’s stated alternatives are retained.

The upper marginal ending after the generator pair has a tall hooked stem, small upper loop, dark foot and adjacent short hook. It is represented graphically rather than forced into a period or identified as a letter. Its function remains uncertain. The lower margin has a separate broad left hook and a long sloping line under on a d’autre part bending toward the cancelled rho-like sign; the approximate geometry is reproduced in an adjacent graphic, not as an underline or a supplied closing parenthesis.

All C deleted passages were checked individually: cancelled epsilon_0-like prefix; cancelled exponent4; three cancelled rho-like factors; cancelled On; lower cancelled tilde-rho-like sign. C contains no inserted macro on this page, and no distinct interlinear lexical insertion was found. The margin notes are separately inventoried.

The actual handwritten page numbers are9 at the head and21 at the bottom left. Formula numbers10,11,12 occur in that physical order. No date is visible. Scan22 is only the editorial identifier. H’s editorial page notice and interpretive notes are not copied as manuscript text, while its omission of footer21 is logged as a real omission.

The whole image and each supplied native overlapping half were read once for this first pass; ten enlarged crops were made once and individually inspected. Root reviewed all ten crops and confirmed the principal readings and nonverbal-mark treatment. No other page, OCR, external source or TeX compilation was used.

The first surviving product in (10) reads epsilon1 = epsilon0 epsilon-infinity^4 rho epsilon0^2 epsilon-infinity^2, after the visible cancellations. Direct inversion gives rho = epsilon-infinity^-4 epsilon0^-1 epsilon1 epsilon-infinity^-2 epsilon0^-2. Thus, under the displayed relation, rho is a word in the epsilon generators. This contradicts the following literal sentence, 'et on trouve comme tantôt que non.' Both the formula and sentence were read on their complete crops and retained; the manuscript's earlier obstruction for sigma generators on scan020 does not give this obstruction for epsilon generators. The corrected implication is recorded only here, as 145-022-rho-is-epsilon-word.

The included check_022_relations.py verifies the algebraic rearrangement by substitution and free cancellation, and checks all 36 products of the six permutations for the parity identity sg(pq)=sg(p)+sg(q) in Z/2. Hence the graph map phi(sigma)=(sigma,sg(sigma)) in (11) is a homomorphism and is injective by its first projection. Its image has six elements in the twelve-element direct product, so has index two. This checks the graph construction; it does not independently prove the stated geometric identification with the stabilizer of P.

Conditional on the stated elements fixing P, their lifts using the trivial path form a homomorphism: the scan017 product rule composes a transformed trivial path with a trivial path, again the trivial path. This checks the stated canonical-lift construction (12) under its stabilizer hypothesis. The text's plain element arrow in (12), missing parentheses in the displayed image of (11), and visible punctuation are preserved without mathematical normalization.

This sheet carries header 9, footer 21 and equations (10)–(12). In the supplied physical order it follows the sheet with equations (13)–(16). Neither its place nor its written numbering has been changed. Two marginal marks are reproduced graphically because their visible strokes are more definite than their textual function.
